label: Same-moment giving from received esse on three readings
summary: Section 11 of docs/notes/sustaining-vs-existential-inertia.md. Three explicit assemblies reach distinct same-moment giving: momentary PSR with the productive bridge, occurrence of the origin relation with term giving, and present receipt with correlativity. The first and third use scoped non-self-giving; the second uses origin irreflexivity. The shared two-moment countermodel grants the explanatory demand, origin accompaniment with an existing distinct originator, and standing receipt at the later moment. It falsifies the corresponding productive bridges there. The passion variant grants correlativity and receipt at onset only. The countermodel also grants concurrence when there is giving, and contact when giving, while the sustaining reading fails. This locates the failure of each proposed implication in the stated formal interpretation. It gives no actual example of a strict giver withdrawing while the same bearer persists. Section 12 tests the negation independently. The all-interval loss law is classically equivalent to survival over inducer-free intervals. No loss inducer occurs in either modeled history. The recipient originates in one and never originates in the other. Holding that history, standing receipt and the momentary explanation fixed, origin-only and sustained giving respectively falsify and satisfy both productive tests. A nonempty conditional origin-essentialist dictionary for the same recipient does not entail existence. The encoded contingency and failure of nature-entailment coexist with either giving assignment. The empty inducer predicate is stipulated and there is no instance of induced loss. Prima facie support for inertia comes from the causal requirement on change and the builder example for causes of becoming. Its extension to existential loss and the classification of withdrawal remain open. Q.104 retains positive warrant for conservation on the strict cause-of-being reading. The open test concerns independently identified withdrawal at the same bearer, not non-origination in another world.
blocker: Q.104 a.1 supports a distinct timeless conserver of participated being. Application still needs coverage of the route receivers and the effect-side GivesAt calibration. Fix the same receiver, its initial origin and independently specified destructive conditions. Establish independently of its later fate that the original source has ceased strict giving. Exclude every other strict giver at the tested moment, including the receiver itself. Does that very receiver survive? An argument for the inertia law must cover existential cessation and justify the absence of an inducer independently of assuming inertia. Row 51 adds a separate same-cause burden if the result is used for sustained giving by a designated cause. The q.8 immediate-contact calibration remains open.
